Accepted at 2026-10-27T16:54:36.182Z by /root/stable_final_audit, actual OpenAI gpt-6-astra (ultra), reviewer session 01a17e3e-2338-7d10-b681-694be00a8b60 and turn 01a17e3e-239e-7da3-a61e-0727bd6f0b31.

I independently accept the prepared stable source at commit 3e296c9ddc3837fb3dd98e79d3c2d07feea31991, tree 209fec6fa38c538d1e6d9ce67c7c3f221e08cc3c. The complete manifest includes 5,032 tracked blobs and modes; SHA-256 27a7658ac8a9711b053708ebd9522694db0e80a21bb6662f3e61583408d5c7d4. The checkout was clean. No blocking source, core-correctness, security or publication-integrity finding remains in the reviewed scope. This permits recording D14 through the existing exact-input rules. It is not a statement that stable packages, final source CI, the stable-tag workflow or the website have already shipped.

Independence and review method

This is an actual separate reviewer session initialized with fork_turns=none under L-65. I verified selected author/reviewer metadata against actual rollout records and the parent dispatch/result. Both actual models are gpt-6-astra; separate sessions and fresh context, not a different model name, establish the approved independence method. The published initialization projection omits encrypted prompt bytes and hidden reasoning. I authored no implementation, gate, workflow, package or repository edit. I created only external observer/audit artifacts, inspected source and retained evidence, and ran pure hash/arithmetic/semantic validation. No browser, Cargo build, benchmark, mutation campaign, workload rerun, workflow dispatch, cancellation, merge, tag or publication was performed by me.

The prior accepted D14 is historical RC3 commit 9c5c0916412d2e398a96513daa9fd9d2966023db, report SHA-256 80a13669faacbdf6227d0bce388a5d8074ef9a5da6c3ac3daadc4c27fc77a382. I read its retained findings and exact-input validator, inspected the material runtime/release delta since that review, and verified focused independent implementation reviews against current source hashes. Historical findings retain their IDs and original severity. The duplicate-warning disposition now becomes resolved from the actual source/test repair. Previous RC3 review is not relabeled as current stable acceptance.

Actual final delta and original qualification

The 55-path delta from executed source 0e116ebf77cb34e15c04d946a706ac0f0556db93 consists of the 27 canonical coordinated version/lock/seed changes, current documentation, finite release policy/tests, the decoder profile and the finite scheduler input inventory. Runtime, compiler/build source, crate source, security harness/corpus and workflows are unchanged from the executed source. Every one of the 27 current version-file hashes matches the independently replayed original canonical version transformer; external dependency graphs were not refreshed. The accepted seven watch files, twelve compile/scheduler files, three hostile-profile files, seven waiver files and three decoder-policy files all match current bytes. Final profile SHA-256 a4279fb3050f70fcbd0eeb64bddd9d1fdfea0c3169a7b8f48b34dc376cd398f7 retains 1,879 inputs and the existing stage/resource policy.

I independently rehashed all 2,198 retained original provider/review files: 323,352,018 bytes, zero mismatches. Their manifest SHA-256 is ef2a156f184c001ab25990a048a3ff09cfb0e6724acb042fea1697ad4bf3e0b0. This is integrity verification of retained provider-authenticated evidence, not a new live API authentication. The five original source planes are terminal success in their retained receipts. CI run 40537713511 attempt 1 uses synthetic checkout 7a531287bacd0f4a2f86d1fcd94944a21b1de503 with tree equality to 0e11: 19 successful jobs, one expected legacy scaffold skip, both 221-case packed platform suites and the full ordinary R17 command. The 620-second R17 observation is not N7.

Original packed P17 run 40537706950 attempt 1 uses actual 0e11 and passed 75/75 checks in 1,303.893 seconds. All eight archives and the original P17 report are preserved; P17 SHA-256 8709c008a71c798c67ea8d1ac566e0f213893151b067302f1e26d6d112e41717. I replayed current performance and security validators against those original data: 2,082 hostile cases, 30 capability controls, nine explicit mount controls, real removed-selector-guard before/mutant/corrected outcomes and 100,000 expression cases per positive control. The security harness hashes match current source. Decoder p95 9.79999999993015 and 27.70000000006985 ms passes the original public-decoder-p95-v1 30 ms policy; no retrospective headroom or rounding was used. Native/mobile/client controls and the real published RC3 performance baseline pass semantic replay. These are original rehearsal results, never stable-tag execution.

Independent installed-consumer receipt SHA-256 997531ef7ac3c4c21a23de6e945db08008ec9b652af46a904b888abb973b50b2 authenticates all eight archives/installed products, 90 native cases (30 per engine), 13 owned groups closed, 12,276/12,288 incremental gzip bytes and 40,704/65,536 group bytes. Retained native-group bytes were independently recompressed by that reader; removed plain scratch outputs have retained inventories/arithmetic, not invented raw bytes. Those facts remain bounded to their original execution.

The soak waiver removes repetition, not the sole security evidence for a changed parser path. I retrieved original provider metadata and all four original logs for scheduled FMIR ASan run 40478618441 attempt 1 at published RC3 source 0cf47cdd6b487543f488f60695f74553282bbe9c. All four actual twenty-minute address-sanitized targets succeeded with original checkout and two unchanged-lock checks per job: parse_raw 149,210,026 runs, parse_body 44,447,734, parse_mutated 15,848,017 and walk 5,953,326, each in 1,201 seconds. The exact Rust/fuzz delta from that source to stable is only internal crate version leaves and fuzz Cargo.lock; no parser/walker/target/corpus/toolchain/workflow source changes. The current original 0e11 CI also independently ran all four packed ASan seed controls, 1,000 inputs each, with successful owned cleanup and explicit zero active soak credit. Those existing unique security controls remain in ordinary CI. This supplies bounded original applicable ASan evidence without a new campaign or a stable soak claim. Full details and original-log hashes are in asan-applicability-review.json.

Original full core mutation run 40516146896 at 79153778 has 326/328 caught, two genuine non-security NaN-key-domain survivors, 169/169 security and 98/98 expression mutations caught, unchanged 4,320 before/after test identities and no equivalents/unqualified results. I rehashed all six supporting applicability pointers and checked unchanged relevant runtime/test/corpus inputs through 0e11 and stable. The separate expression setup timeout and cancelled whole nightly workflow remain cancelled/incomplete; this is applicability of the completed core campaign and separate original P17 security proof, not a fabricated full nightly success or router/server-wide mutation proof.

Root's complete release-helper integration command, ruby scripts/check-release-workflow.rb --self-test under the release runtime, passed 594/594 tests with zero fail/skip/cancel/todo; I authenticated the raw stdout SHA-256 d9c4684336bf5ab059d5892f84b4a396f807f4cf3a255a13f2caa721c653123b and empty stderr. Its outer receipt is 77.839 seconds. The subsequent frozen profile/gate changes were separately inspected. The preserved research check reports 49 inputs, 105 questions and 57 acceptance IDs. No original ledger or failed observation was rewritten.

Maintainer decision and security boundary

The actual recorded instruction is “ok in in regards to soak and all those other stuff, skip, just streamline to the finish line, skip what you can that does not compromise security and get 3.2 released”. The committed assistant transcription at docs/release/3.2-STREAMLINED-RELEASE.json has SHA-256 f1ff0da25d3771916c4326b40141ca8220c81a3900af76a9b3ccb49482726b8e and explicitly identifies that it is not an independently signed artifact. The parent supplied this current human authorization. Only soak is individually named; skipping further N7 repetition, extra RC publication solely for soak and a staged production rollback exercise is the documented application of the instruction to skip non-security work. Existing rollback capability and real deployment verification remain required.

The new path is finite to final 3.2.0 with exactly two paired waived gates and exact decision/reference/hash. Changed decision bytes, another version, waived security/audit gates, mixed deferral or missing counterpart fail closed. Both publication preflight and DS12 require the actual final-source D14 and committed decision. DS12 retains original source-bound P17, all four audit assets and the decision. The existing tag-only workflow still requires successful exact-commit push/main CI, locked pack, three engines, P17, artifact verification and protected crates/npm OIDC publishing. The waiver supplies no credential, no generic environment bypass and no changed archive allowance. Stable record recovery/placeholder handling remains separate.

The separate authorized decoder limit is explicitly 30.7 ms only for 3.2.0/positive rc.N reports that identify the new profile. Historical profiles retain 30 ms. All shapes, 40 samples, five warmups, four-times CPU slowdown, nearest-rank calculation, actual values, CSP/Trusted Types, zero initial writes and refusal controls remain unchanged. Its semantics do not convert old failures or missing checks into passes.

All non-audit source gate dispositions and wording were settled before the reviewed commit. Audit alone remains pending. The candidate/measurements rows correctly cite prior applicable source execution while preserving mandatory actual stable-tag recomputation. Final supported-profile acceptance preserves the original Mac/iPhone scope, rather than pretending a new device session occurred. Website deployment/live docs/download acceptance is a later required action after stable publication, with no interim preview update. No new soak requirement or approval step is invented.
